scenes.text: Damascus steel blades were famed for being *razor sharp* and remarkably tough.
Their surface showed *rippled, watery patterns* that no one could mistake.
The steel was made from *wootz,* ingots produced in India and traded across the Middle East.
Then, around the *1700s,* the original method of making it faded away.
Modern metallurgists still debate *exactly how* those blades were forged.
Follow for more *lost secrets* of history.
